description.text:
Completed-vector storage internal to C2C, not an SRF stall mechanism.
DEPTH must be >= 2. No empty-to-output combinational fall-through.

Vector-level peer transport for the normal path, not a physical link.
A valid input available after edge C is visible at RX after edge C+L.
LINK_LATENCY must be >= 1; every stage advances each cycle, even bubbles.

Stateless FIFO-head rendezvous. Both upstream queues retain their heads
until pop; their heads are consumed together at the Replay sampling edge.
This is the proposed minimal Receive/ready-vector pairing contract.

Complete received vectors only. Destination selection belongs to Receive.
DEPTH >= 1. No empty-to-output combinational fall-through.

Normal-path expansion of one complete vector into four diagonal SRF
producer candidates. Collision handling and SRF selection are external.

description.text: Four-tile, normal-path diagonal gather. Stream selection is external.

Vector-level admission control between the completed FIFO and peer flight.
This is deliberately not a beat-level PHY serializer.  One accepted vector
holds one credit through serializer occupancy, link flight, and RX-ready
residence; the paired Receive pop supplies credit_return_i.

Single logical DMA Store-lane control context.
This block accepts already-decoded descriptor semantics.  It intentionally
does not decode a 192-bit descriptor slot, define an ICU codec, generate
addresses, or issue external-storage requests.  The fixed P_LANE_INDEX
identifies the logical DMA lane; it is distinct from an ordinary SRF stream
selector even when a static schedule uses the same numeric value.

description.text:
QCTL load manager preserves the external logical Pool-address contract while
converting accepted partitions and records into explicit Relay packets.

One Hemisphere QCTL Relay chain. Its seven stages mirror Program Distribution
and terminate all Queue traffic locally before RUN begins.

One physical QCTL Relay stage. Non-local packets cross a registered Transit
FIFO; local partitions and records terminate in the shared regional store.

Test-only payload utility, not the architectural Receive/FIFO endpoint.
Selected TX segments -> peer payload -> RX candidates. The testbench must
supply rx_stream_idx_i with the peer payload and hold it through capture.
No SRF attachment, command pairing, slot mapping, or wrapper state.

Pure combinational attachment: Replay tile t -> West sreg13 superlane t.
One shared valid covers the entire 64-bit segment. No payload/control state.

Thin RX connection wrapper. The source respects FIFO capacity; the external
Receive-command queue holds its head until rx_cmd_pop_o. No TX metadata port.

One-way peer attachment between independent source/destination hemispheres.
This wrapper adds no state. Receive, not Send, selects the destination stream.

Stateless connection wrapper. Input tile t is [t*64 +: 64]; stream
selection is external. Gather completion and the peer boundary are payload-only.

Stateless with respect to SRF payload: this adapter observes East sreg13,
selects one C2C-attached stream per diagonal tile, and returns the matching
segment consume.  Only the selector/valid delay line is local control state.

Stateless conversion from the formal MEM machine code to the private
32-bit Native control word. Legal but unimplemented operations fail closed.

description.text:
Phase 2B wrapper: a bank-local, zero-cycle command conversion in front of
the unchanged Phase 2A MEM/SRF data plane.

DMA-1C Store-only composition.  MEM and the DMA TX attachment share one
ordinary SRF hemisphere.  The wrapper owns no SRF payload state: leaf state
remains exclusively inside ftlpu_sr_superlane_col_dir.
The Store attachment is the existing C2C TX tap in External-storage DMA
mode: East sreg13, E0..E7, and local consumer slot 0.  It is deliberately
not a peer transport, descriptor engine, or external-memory protocol.

Phase 2A standalone MEM/SRF data-plane integration variant.
The adapter in this module is purely combinational.  The authoritative SRF
owns all stream state; MEM only observes current boundary state and produces
consume/inject candidates.  MEM uses two independent local candidate slots (Q06=A).

One independent south-to-north command pipeline for a logical MEM bank.
Native command bit 30 selects a one-cycle (0) or three-cycle (1) hop.
tile0 sees the current south command combinationally. Each later tile has
one execution register and two extra registers used only by long commands.

One physical MEM storage leaf for a fixed
(hemisphere, mem_slice, bank, superlane) coordinate.
The SRAM array is single-port: at most one complete-row Read or Write is
accepted in a cycle. Reset clears only control/output state; SRAM contents
are intentionally not reset.

Stateless c7 raw primitive to native canonical command conversion.
This is not the legacy 47-bit packet format and adds no issue register.
The current parameterized input ABI extends c7 with delay3 in bit 30.
Set P_ALLOW_DELAY3=0 only when checking the frozen original c7 encoding.

Generic MEM group located between a left boundary (sreg[g]) and a right
boundary (sreg[g+1]). Four slices share the same cycle-start boundary state.

description.text:
One MEM hemisphere: 52 slices arranged as 13 fixed groups between 14 MEM
SR boundaries. This wrapper routes cycle-start state and candidates only; it
does not implement SR propagation or next-state commit.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE / INTERNAL INTEGRATION INTERFACE:
one logical bank composed of independent single-port SRAM leaves and a
command pipeline with per-command one/three-cycle hops (native bit 30).
This wrapper adds no storage and performs no bank-global arbitration.

One MEM slice contains two fully independent logical banks. The Slice/SR
boundary is abstract: it observes only the current boundary SR state and
emits consume/injection candidates. It does not instantiate or arbitrate SR.

One output column: LANES FP32 adders, two 1RW banks, no operand feedback.
Compiler works backwards from the operand capture edge T:
command launch T-3, read service T-2, B and array A available after T-1,
A1/T A2/T+1 A3/T+2, writeback or common output register T+3.
NO array-A registers precede A1. STORE uses the existing three-stage
passthrough, giving all writes the same phase and preserving read->write D=5.

Independent instruction queue for the accumulator/storage result positions.
In lpu_mxm_core, position c is Superlane c at the left array edge.
No automatic launch, operand feedback, destination routing or dynamic stalls.

BF16 DAZ dot product, two multiply stages plus seven reduction stages.
Fixed nine register stages, II=1. No FP32 conversion before reduction.
Alignment truncates magnitudes toward zero before two's-complement sign.
Separate enqueue and compiler-timed launch; no autonomous rescheduling.
Independent queues; count-free compute beats and fixed-mode weight loads.

Complete new BF16 array + independently scheduled FP32 accumulator/storage
backend. Top results return down/left to local Superlane accumulators.
Raw top and returned-left buses are exposed separately; no stream formatter.

Independent, compiler-launched parameter-load and dequantization queues.
Both streams propagate at the same row interval as weight-load commands.
One dequant command must meet every actual INT8 input beat, including all
MATRIX beats. No count expansion, automatic launch, stall or retry.

Three register stages, II=1: align; add/subtract; normalize/RNE/pack.
FP32 subnormals are preserved. NaNs are canonicalized. No ready/stall path.
This first implementation uses exact leading-zero detection, not LZA.

New MXM boundary: queued control + physical Supercell array. FP32 column
outputs connect to the independently instructed two-bank backend.
Row zero is bottom. Stream selection occurs upstream using row commands.

One common registered output stage for FP32 passthrough and BF16 RNE.
A 32-bit lane carries either FP32 or zero-extended BF16 in bits [15:0].
This is the core interface, not final stream packing or destination routing.

Static diagonal result-return fabric. Row zero is bottom, column zero left.
A top result from column c descends to row c, then travels left to that
Superlane's accumulator. Only positions r>=c contain return registers.
Off-diagonal positions have TWO independent streams, not an arbitrated mux.
One register per visited position, including the diagonal/left endpoint:
(ROWS-1-c) downward stages + (c+1) leftward stages = ROWS, for every c.

description.text:
Weight-stationary Supercell. No dynamic scheduling or backpressure.
One activation vector broadcasts to every output group on the same edge.
Group n computes sum_k activation[k]*weight[buffer][n][k], with TERMS
multipliers per group. All groups have the same dot/partial output phase.
Activation, buffer ID, tag and valid forward right through ONE register;
the compiler arranges lower-partial inputs at simultaneous dot-valid.

Load-only INT8 -> BF16 conversion. D1 subtract/decode, D2 exact 8x8
product and normalization-shift detection. D3 shift/RNE feeds the Supercell
weight register, the third register boundary (no extra output register).
Parameter commands load paired scale/zero buffers; D1 snapshots their values.
Weight and parameter commands consume separate fixed byte streams. No general
FP32 multiplier, integer-to-BF16 intermediate, LUT or division is used.

One combinational FP32 Newton multiply stage. Finite operands use one
inferred unsigned 24x24 significand multiply inside fp32_multiply_rne.
Two instances keep the two Newton products on separate dedicated 24x24
significand datapaths:
  stage 1: m*y0
  stage 2: y0*(2-m*y0)
The current special-ALU issue controller remains single-outstanding; its
admission policy can be relaxed separately. The module boundary keeps the
two physical demand points explicit for DC.

Fused FP32 RSQRT Newton correction:
  correction = 1.5 - 0.5*m*y_squared
m and y_squared are positive finite normal FP32 values on this internal
path. Their 24x24 significand product remains at full 48-bit precision,
is aligned with 1.5 in Q55, subtracted, and rounded to FP32 only once.

C3-class Log continuation. A single multiplier and a single Horner adder
are selected by phase; low formats bypass unneeded polynomial stages.
LUT row = {ln(c) UQ0.28, 1/c UQ1.21}, c=1+address/64.

parameters.raw:
// Number of coefficient rows; COEFFICIENT_WIDTH is bits per half-row and ADDRESS_WIDTH is bits per row index.
	parameter integer ENTRY_COUNT = 64

description.text:
One physical LUT SRAM for one special-function type. The slope/intercept
pair stays in one row so synthesis sees one SRAM, not
independent k/b memories or an inferred multi-read array. COEFFICIENT_WIDTH
is 13 for each packed half of the EXP UQ1.25 base and 16 for the RECIP or
RSQRT UQ1.15 coefficients.
待确认：RTL 结构显示 3 个输入、1 个输出，并包含 0 个子模块实例模板。该说明仅来自结构计数，未推断功能。

Fixed-point RECIP LUT interpolation for y0 = b - k*dx.
A 64-entry table consumes the top six fraction bits as its address. The
remaining fraction bits are a right-aligned residual:
  BF16: 1 bit / 2^7, FP16: 4 bits / 2^10, FP32: 17 bits / 2^23.
k and b are physically UQ1.15. Narrow formats use RNE-reduced UQ1.9 and
UQ1.12 values. One 16x17 unsigned multiply is shared by zero extension;
the aligned subtraction uses one signed 40-bit datapath.

Fixed-point RSQRT LUT interpolation for y0 = b - k*dx.
The 64-entry address is {exponent parity, five high fraction bits}.
The parity-dependent factor of two is folded into the stored slope, leaving
right-aligned residuals of 2/5/18 bits for BF16/FP16/FP32 respectively.
k and b are physically UQ1.15. Narrow formats use RNE-reduced UQ1.9 and
UQ1.12 values. One zero-extended 16x18 multiply and one signed 40-bit
subtraction are shared by all formats.

One shared 27-bit significand add/subtract datapath, split at the FP16
boundary: 14 low bits and 13 high bits. The extra result bit is the carry,
not a 28th full-adder bit. BF16/FP16 isolate the high group completely.

assignments.expression: assign normal_arithmetic_enable = enable_i && ((data_format_i == VXM_FORMAT_FP16) || (data_format_i == VXM_FORMAT_BF16) || (data_format_i == VXM_FORMAT_FP32)) && !lhs_nan_i && !rhs_nan_i && !lhs_inf_i && !rhs_inf_i && !lhs_zero_i && !rhs_zero_i;

description.text:
One format-selected FP16/BF16/FP32 add/subtract cone.
The format MUX and operand isolation are deliberately before the shared
significand datapath. Near subtraction uses one grouped leading-zero
encoder and one format-masked variable left shifter.

Shared FP16/BF16/FP32 magnitude and ordered comparator.
Operand format decode, classification and DAZ are performed once by the
Basic-ALU front end. This block only compares the resulting fields. FP16
and BF16 use the complete low 15-bit comparator. FP32 adds a high 16-bit
comparison and consults the same low comparator only when the high parts
are equal.

One logical left shifter shared by FP16, BF16 and FP32 normalization.
The format mask isolates unused high input bits and truncates the result.

parameters.raw:
// Total multiplier coefficient bits versus fractional-bit counts in the stored and format-reduced coefficients.
	parameter integer COEFFICIENT_WIDTH = 26

description.text:
Shared unsigned coefficient multiplier for LUT-based special functions.
The default EXP instance is a physical 26x24 multiply. Parameters also
permit narrower coefficient formats while retaining one physical datapath.
Narrow formats round the stored coefficient to their selected internal
precision, right-align the
active value significand, and zero-fill every unused high bit:
  BF16 : UQ1.9  (10 bits) x  8-bit significand
  FP16 : UQ1.12 (13 bits) x 11-bit significand
  FP32 : UQ1.25 (26 bits) x 24-bit significand
This deliberately leaves the multiplier architecture to synthesis/DC.

Private LUT set for one Tile/Superlane. Every {function, Lane} owns

Programming broadcasts identical contents to the Lane replicas.
EXP rows are 26 bits, RECIP/RSQRT rows 32 bits, and Log rows 50 bits.

assign { reasm_rsp_error_o, reasm_rsp_id_o, reasm_rsp_last_o, reasm_rsp_keep_o, reasm_rsp_data_o } = response_dequeue_data;

assign frontend_fault_code_o = ((|mem_frontend_fault) || (|mxm_frontend_fault) || (|sxm_frontend_fault)) ? FAULT_FRONTEND : ((ENABLE_QCTL && qctl_fault_o) ? FAULT_QCTL : FAULT_NONE);
assign stream_conflict_o[HEMISPHERE_INDEX] = mem_stream_conflict | sxm_stream_conflict | mxm_stream_conflict | vxm_stream_conflict;
assign fault_o = manager_fault || east_chain_fault || west_chain_fault || event_fault || fabric_fault || (|endpoint_fault_i);

policy.statement: Physical Architecture 展示功能单元、hemisphere 拓扑与数据/控制关系；RTL Hierarchy 保留源码层次。
policy.accuracyStatement: 参考图只决定表达形式。实例数、阵列参数、generate 范围与接口证据均来自当前 RTL；未确认项保留表达式或 Needs Review。
policy.floorplanDisclaimer: 此视图不是最终芯片 floorplan，也不表示后端物理坐标或实际布线。

regions.name: External Program Memory Boundary
regions.basis: Current RTL exposes a generic Program DMA command/response boundary. No DDR controller, DDR memory model, or standard AXI five-channel adapter is instantiated in the authoritative RTL snapshot.

regions.name: Program Load and Distributed Instruction Control
regions.basis: The display separates the RTL-confirmed Instruction DMA, response reassembly, hemisphere distribution and FU-local instruction-control path. Relative placement is architectural, not floorplan data.

regions.name: West Hemisphere
regions.basis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX 1 is selected by gen_west_host_column; left/right presentation is a functional-topology view, not floorplan coordinates.

regions.name: Central / On-chip Bisection
regions.basis: The single VXM instance is outside the two-hemisphere generate loop and connects both MEM sides.

regions.name: East Hemisphere
regions.basis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX 0 is selected by gen_east_host_column; left/right presentation is a functional-topology view, not floorplan coordinates.

blocks.function: Native-default MEM with 104 bank-local instruction frontend and direct issue paths south of the bank array. Each path emits a MEM64 command northward into its logical bank control column; legality checks, private Native32 adaptation and bidirectional stream data remain explicit.
blocks.placementBasis: The else branch is named gen_west_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: Two-instance generate loop with an RTL-confirmed hemisphere selector.

controlPath: 104 bank-local instruction frontend + direct issue paths
structure.namingNote: USE_NATIVE_MEM defaults to 1. Native32 exists only beyond the adapter boundary. The disabled Legacy Compatibility branch maps Bank0 into 52 old issue paths and turns Bank1 issue into an explicit sticky compatibility fault.

blocks.function: Formal Program endpoint with separate 64-event CTRL and EXEC calendars, absolute-cycle ROW issue, Triangle execution and bidirectional stream boundary.
blocks.placementBasis: The else branch is named gen_west_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: lpu_sxm_native_subsystem is instantiated by each Hemisphere of the formal FU cluster.

structure.namingNote: The formal Program route instantiates lpu_sxm_native_subsystem once per Hemisphere. The older lpu_sxm_subsystem is a separate typed batch WriteTap path; raw416 is independent core compatibility. SXM QCTL has no formal endpoint.

blocks.function: Two local current-core MXM engines sharing the hemisphere stream boundary. Each owns five ICU streams: Load, Compute, Dequant, Param Load and Backend, with direct Scheduler-to-native-port issue.
blocks.placementBasis: The else branch is named gen_west_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: Nested generate loop instantiates two current MXM subsystems per hemisphere.

controlPath: Direct native command port · no Instruction Queue

blocks.function: Native-default MEM with 104 bank-local instruction frontend and direct issue paths south of the bank array. Each path emits a MEM64 command northward into its logical bank control column; legality checks, private Native32 adaptation and bidirectional stream data remain explicit.
blocks.placementBasis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX == 0 selects gen_east_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: Two-instance generate loop with an RTL-confirmed hemisphere selector.

controlPath: 104 bank-local instruction frontend + direct issue paths
structure.namingNote: USE_NATIVE_MEM defaults to 1. Native32 exists only beyond the adapter boundary. The disabled Legacy Compatibility branch maps Bank0 into 52 old issue paths and turns Bank1 issue into an explicit sticky compatibility fault.

blocks.placementBasis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX == 0 selects gen_east_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: lpu_sxm_native_subsystem is instantiated by each Hemisphere of the formal FU cluster.

structure.namingNote: The formal Program route instantiates lpu_sxm_native_subsystem once per Hemisphere. The older lpu_sxm_subsystem is a separate typed batch WriteTap path; raw416 is independent core compatibility. SXM QCTL has no formal endpoint.

blocks.placementBasis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX == 0 selects gen_east_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

controlPath: Direct native command port · no Instruction Queue

blocks.function: Single vector execution subsystem bridging stream traffic from both MEM hemispheres.
blocks.placementBasis: The single instance is outside the hemisphere loop and its ports cover both hemisphere slices; “central” is a functional-topology placement, not a floorplan coordinate.

rtlMappings.basis: Single subsystem instance connected to both halves of the MEM stream vectors.

blocks.function: Intended external storage for program-image bytes. This is an architecture endpoint only: no DDR controller or memory model is instantiated in the authoritative RTL snapshot.
blocks.instanceCountExpression: No DDR/DRAM module or memory model found in current RTL/filelist
blocks.placementBasis: lpu_top exposes a generic Program DMA request/response boundary, while the testbench supplies response beats. The external memory controller and protocol adapter remain outside the current RTL.

rtlMappings.basis: Architecture placeholder; no synthesized RTL instance exists.

structure.namingNote: DDR is an external endpoint, not an RTL-confirmed on-chip SRAM. Program Transfer begins after the generic DMA response crosses the top-level boundary.

blocks.function: Protocol boundary between the generic Program DMA request/response contract and an external memory fabric. Standard AXI AR/AW/W/R/B channels are not present in the current RTL.
blocks.instanceCountExpression: No AXI/C2C adapter module found; only generic program_dma_cmd_* / program_dma_rsp_* top ports exist
blocks.placementBasis: The generic command/response boundary is RTL-confirmed. Mapping it to AXI or C2C is a future integration decision and is intentionally not fabricated here.

rtlMappings.basis: Boundary placeholder backed by top-level generic Program DMA ports, not a protocol adapter instance.

parameters: Response: data[255:0], keep[31:0], last, id[7:0], error

structure.namingNote: The label names the intended integration boundary; it does not assert a current AXI implementation.

blocks.function: RTL-confirmed read-request and response-buffer engine for program-image transport, with ordered outstanding-ID tracking and terminal fault detection.
blocks.placementBasis: lpu_program_transfer_path explicitly instantiates lpu_instruction_dma and binds its generic external command/response ports to the Program DMA boundary.

rtlMappings.basis: Explicit RTL instance in the Program Load subsystem.

structure.namingNote: This module emits a generic read contract; it is not itself an AXI master or a DDR controller.

blocks.displayName: Program Load System + Program Distribution System
blocks.function: Main RTL chain: Instruction DMA → response buffer → Assembler/Reassembler → Program Word FIFO → Distributor Elastic Stage → West/East Relay chains → FU frontend/local iMEM. The central VXM route branches directly from the Distributor elastic head and bypasses both Relay chains.
blocks.instanceCountExpression: top siblings: u_program_load_system + u_program_distribute_system + u_fu_subsystems; East R0–R6 + West R0–R6 = 14 integrated two-entry Relay stages
blocks.placementBasis: lpu_top directly instantiates Program Load, Program Distribution and the FU Cluster as three siblings. Program Distribution is not nested in the Cluster. Its two generated seven-stage Relay chains connect through top-level Program buses to fourteen MEM Local Program Ports without a Hemisphere 7-to-1 round-robin.

structure.namingNote: The command descriptor store is an RTL register array, not instruction-payload SRAM. Program Load, Program Distribution and FU Cluster are direct lpu_top siblings. VXM branches directly from the Distributor elastic head and bypasses Relay. MEM and MXM local frontends are integrated. SXM Target 5/6 uses the R6 Outer Local path and the native CTRL/EXEC calendars; VXM still has a boundary without a formal local issue path.

blocks.function: Load Manager → East/West QCTL Relay chains → 14 regional Stores → 228 FU-local Endpoint readers and five-state Controllers → 208 MEM and 20 MXM Scheduler Cycle Counters. Runtime Event, SYNC, NOTIFY and MEM_PACKET traffic stays on the independent Fabric; VXM and SXM are not formal QCTL endpoints.
blocks.placementBasis: The cluster conditionally instantiates one lpu_qctl_global_subsystem. It owns one Load Manager, two seven-stage Relay chains and shared runtime resources; Queue Endpoint and Controller instances are generated beside MEM/MXM Schedulers. ENABLE_QCTL defaults to 0, so the structure is integrated but default-gated.

rtlMappings.basis: Global load-time QCTL routing and regional storage under the conditional generate branch.

controlPath: Regional Directory + Record Array + Valid Bitmap
MEM local counters ×208 + MXM local counters ×20
structure.namingNote: RTL integrated, default gated (ENABLE_QCTL=0). RUN reads the owning regional Store directly; there is no central Pool refill or per-Queue Record Cache. Formal endpoint numbering covers MEM and MXM only; VXM and SXM have no direct QCTL counter-control connection. MEM_PACKET retirement is packet/data-movement completion, not SRAM Commit. VCS results are scoped module/integration evidence, not a complete Program Load-to-FU runtime system pass.

nodes.displayName: MEM West · Native MEM + SRF Architecture
nodes.description: Three parallel views describe the current main-branch RTL: 104 Bank-local macro frontends issue directly into MEM64/Native32 command adaptation, the Native array owns 13 Groups / 52 Slices / 104 Banks / 416 SRAM leaves, and lpu_mem_srf_integration connects the MEM array beside the independent SRF hemisphere fabric.

sourceEvidence.basis: Current subsystem boundary and generated Bank-local frontend ownership.
The integration module instantiates SRF and Native MEM as parallel children.

nodes.description: Each logical Bank owns Local iMEM → Fetch → Word FIFO → Macro Decoder → Context FIFO → Macro Scheduler. The Scheduler drives mem_issue_valid/instruction/cycle directly; current main-branch RTL has no independent lpu_mem_instruction_queue.

sourceEvidence.basis: gen_bank_frontend instantiates one complete u_frontend per logical Bank.
u_macro_frontend binds mem_issue_* directly to the local frontend output.

nodes.description: Program words are stored in a Bank-local 96-bit iMEM, fetched in order and decoded/scheduled by the macro frontend. Program writes accept strobe 0111; invalid strobe/address raises FAULT_LOAD and inhibits the write.

sourceEvidence.basis: Each generated Bank lane instantiates lpu_mem_local_imem_frontend.
The macro frontend is the terminal instruction-generation stage.

nodes.description: Word FIFO → lpu_mem_macro_decoder → Context FIFO → lpu_mem_macro_scheduler → direct mem_issue_* handoff.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro frontend instantiates only the two FIFOs, decoder and scheduler; no Instruction Queue follows the Scheduler.

nodes.description: One adapter per Bank-local issue lane validates the public 64-bit MEM instruction and emits a private 32-bit Native command only for legal implemented operations. Standard adapted commands keep bit30 clear and therefore use the one-cycle control hop.

sourceEvidence.basis: gen_adapter creates one lpu_mem_command_adapter per {slice,bank} lane.
Only legal implemented instructions emit Native32; the standard mapping does not set long-hop bit30.

nodes.description: One Hemisphere contains 13 Groups × 4 Slices × 2 Banks × 4 independent superlane leaves. The active top-level depth is 8192 rows per 64-bit behavioral leaf.

sourceEvidence.basis: The default USE_NATIVE_MEM path instantiates lpu_mem_srf_command_integration.

nodes.description: lpu_mem_srf_integration instantiates Native MEM and ftlpu_sr_hemisphere_fabric beside one another. Four superlanes × 32 streams × 64-bit segments are carried in each of two directions across sixteen active SRF columns.

sourceEvidence.basis: Boundary b maps directly to SRF column b for MEM boundaries 0..13.
SRF fabric and Native MEM are instantiated as parallel children.

nodes.description: The 12-state FSM expands packed Macro words into complete scheduling Contexts. OUTPUT_CONTEXT holds valid until handshake; when all Macros are consumed, IDLE self-loops with done_o asserted.

nodes.description: Checks target, opcode, iteration counts, intervals, strides, address range and deadline before admission.

Selects exactly one Context whose next issue cycle equals the current schedule cycle and raises timing/conflict faults otherwise.
mem_issue_valid_o, 64-bit instruction and 32-bit cycle leave the Scheduler directly; ready advances or retires the selected Context.
Implemented READ and WRITE operations produce a 32-bit Native command for the matching Bank lane.
GATHER and SCATTER are legal but unsupported; retired opcode 2 is illegal. Neither enters Native execution.
Two independent direction fabrics each contain sixteen columns, four superlanes and thirty-two streams of 64-bit segments.
Boundary b maps directly to SRF column b. Thirteen MEM groups occupy the intervals between fourteen shared boundaries.
East Write consumes the left group boundary; East Read injects at the right group boundary.
West Write consumes the right group boundary; West Read injects at the left group boundary.

sourceEvidence.basis: Group instantiates four mem_slice modules.

nodes.description: One mem_logical_bank_column contains exactly one command Control Column plus four independent 64-bit superlane SRAM leaves. It adds no extra storage or bank-global arbitration.

sourceEvidence.basis: Each bank instantiates one mem_logical_bank_column.

nodes.description: Native32 command enters from the south. Tile0 observes it combinationally; later tiles select either a one-cycle short hop (bit30=0) or a three-cycle long hop (bit30=1).

sourceEvidence.basis: tile0 executes the south command without a stage0 register.

nodes.displayName: SXM Native East · Integrated · Native ROW Architecture
nodes.description: Formal FU-cluster SXM path: R6 Outer Local Program records enter native CTRL and EXEC calendars. Absolute-cycle events drive ROW CAP/P/RUN in the Triangle core, with MEM and MXM streams passing through the SXM boundary.

The formal FU cluster binds Program Valid/Ready/Error and the complete 13-bit Destination, 17-bit Address and 128-bit Data to one native subsystem per Hemisphere. Target 5 is CTRL, target 6 is EXEC; local index must be zero.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_sxm_subsystem is the native Program endpoint inside each Hemisphere.

nodes.description: Stores 128-bit CTRL payload plus timing word per event. At the selected absolute schedule cycle it issues one CTRL event to the ROW core.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_ctrl_calendar stores target 5 records.

nodes.description: Independent EXEC table issues CAP, P and RUN controls at absolute cycles. CTRL and EXEC may issue together.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_exec_calendar stores target 6 records.

nodes.description: The native subsystem is a real bidirectional stream hop. East inner receives MEM; East outer feeds MXM. West outer receives MXM; West inner feeds MEM.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_stream_boundary connects the native ROW selectors and the two stream edges.

nodes.description: sxm_triangle_full_core owns the formal native ROW path. Its ROW frontend and shared storage process CAP, then a one-stage P pipeline, then finite RUN output. T=4 gives ten left-aligned 8×8×32-bit slots per Hemisphere.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_execution receives native CTRL/EXEC events.

nodes.description: Four source rings have depths 1, 2, 3 and 4; each slot is an 8×8×32-bit matrix. Two Hemispheres therefore instantiate twenty slots.
lpu_sxm_subsystem retains the typed batch Triangle MEM Adapter and WriteTap Completion path. It is not the Program endpoint instantiated by the formal FU cluster.
The full core retains raw 416-bit compatibility inputs, but they are tied to zero on the formal native Program route. Do not interpret raw416 as Program payload.

VCS final unified regression: five scenarios and 2787 checks, including native matrix/vector timing, early-P fault and Reset reload. A joint production CModel-to-RTL trace comparison has not been run; SXM QCTL endpoint is not integrated.
Current integrated RTL path: lpu_mxm_subsystem instantiates the parameterized lpu_mxm_core. The legacy slice/shared-accumulator architecture is not retained in this view.

sourceEvidence.basis: lpu_mxm_subsystem explicitly instantiates lpu_mxm_core as u_execution.
The core explicitly owns u_frontend, u_result_return and u_backend.

nodes.displayName: Five-Stream MXM ICU Frontends · Direct Native Issue
nodes.description: Load, Compute, Dequant, Param Load and Backend each own local iMEM, Fetch, Word FIFO, an independent instance of the shared Decoder architecture, Context FIFO and a stream-specific Scheduler. Every Scheduler drives its matching native command port directly through QCTL endpoint gating; no post-Scheduler Instruction Queue or Local Coordinator exists.

sourceEvidence.basis: gen_frontend generates all five stream-local paths and binds their issue handshakes directly to native command ports.
Word FIFO → shared Decoder core → Context FIFO → stream Scheduler → direct issue handshake.

nodes.displayName: Shared MXM Macro Decoder Architecture · 12 States
nodes.description: One RTL implementation is instantiated five times. State, dictionary and Macro-count progress are independent for Load, Compute, Dequant, Param Load and Backend.

sourceEvidence.basis: The shared core declares the twelve architectural states.
Each frontend instance owns its own Decoder core instance.

nodes.description: Local iMEM → Fetch → Word FIFO → shared Decoder instance → Context FIFO → Load Scheduler → QCTL gate → load_command native ready/valid port.
Local iMEM → Fetch → Word FIFO → shared Decoder instance → Context FIFO → Compute Scheduler → QCTL gate → compute_command native ready/valid port.
Local iMEM → Fetch → Word FIFO → shared Decoder instance → Context FIFO → Dequant Scheduler → QCTL gate → dequant_command native ready/valid port.
Local iMEM → Fetch → Word FIFO → shared Decoder instance → Context FIFO → Param Load Scheduler → QCTL gate → param_load_command native ready/valid port.
Local iMEM → Fetch → Word FIFO → shared Decoder instance → Context FIFO → Backend Scheduler → QCTL gate → backend_command native ready/valid port.
Wait for and validate the global control word.
Load Delta dictionary entries.
Initialize absolute cycle and address state.
Decode the current Run header and length.
Decode and validate the instruction template.
Run boundary; self-loop with done_o asserted when the Macro queue count is zero.
Decode Delta prefix and select dictionary or escape source.
Read the selected dictionary Delta.
Read Compact or Wide escape Delta.
Apply cycle/address/operand Delta to the Context state.
Hold the decoded Context until the Context FIFO handshake.

sourceEvidence.basis: Current subsystem execution instance is lpu_mxm_core.

nodes.description: Queued Compute/Load/Param/Dequant control drives a 4×4 Supercell array. Activations and weights move left-to-right; FP32 partial sums move from Row0 upward.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_frontend is the core compute-array boundary.

nodes.description: Each top-column result descends to its diagonal row and then travels left to the matching Superlane. Every column path contains exactly four registered stages.

sourceEvidence.basis: Static down/left routing and equal ROWS-cycle paths are stated and implemented in RTL.

nodes.description: Four independent columns each contain eight FP32 adders, two single-port logical accumulator banks and a shared FP32/BF16 output stage.

SXM accepts target 5/6 into native CTRL/EXEC calendars; VXM still has a boundary with Ready low and no local adapter.

nodes.displayName: QCTL Distributed Relay Store · 228 Formal Endpoints
nodes.description: Load-time QCTL records pass through a Load Manager and two seven-stage Relay chains into fourteen regional Stores. During RUN, one FU-local Endpoint per MEM/MXM Scheduler reads its owning Store directly and feeds a five-state Controller. No central Pool refill or per-Queue Record Cache remains.

sourceEvidence.basis: One Load Manager routes into East and West Relay chains.
Global storage is separated from FU-local Queue-reader and Controller state.

nodes.description: Preserves the external Partition Base/Count/Generation and logical Record Load contract, then converts each accepted operation into a Queue/Offset/Generation packet for Relay routing.

sourceEvidence.basis: Load Manager validates Partition and Record writes before packet emission.
u_load_manager is the only load-time packet source.

nodes.description: Queue ID selects a Hemisphere and one of seven regional Relay stages. Each Relay combines packet forwarding with a Queue Directory, a 64-entry Record Array, a matching Valid Bitmap and a two-entry Transit FIFO.

sourceEvidence.basis: East and West lpu_qctl_relay_chain instances.
Each chain generates R0 through R6.
The Record Array and record_valid_q bitmap are Relay-local.

nodes.description: MEM 0..103 + MXM0/1 five-stream endpoints. Packets move stage by stage with Valid/Ready backpressure; the owning Relay consumes local packets and forwards all later-stage packets.
Owns sixteen local MEM Queue slots and forwards packets for later stages.
Owns sixteen local MEM Queue slots and forwards packets for later stages.

Owns the final eight MEM Queue slots plus ten local MXM stream slots: eighteen directory entries addressed by a five-bit local index.

The same storage and validity contract is repeated in every R0–R6 stage.
Valid + Local Base + Count + Generation for locally owned Queues.
Stores the physical Records and is intentionally not reset.
Cleared by Reset/Program Clear and set only by a legal Record handshake.
Buffers later-stage packets and propagates backpressure without reordering.

One lpu_qctl_endpoint sits beside each MEM/MXM Scheduler. It owns Queue-local Head Index/Generation and refuses to present an unconfigured, out-of-range, unwritten or stale-generation Record as valid.

sourceEvidence.basis: One Endpoint is generated beside each MEM Scheduler.
Five Endpoint readers are generated per MXM subsystem.

nodes.description: Selects the current Queue-relative Record and current Program generation.
Missing or invalid expected data becomes an explicit local fault, never an ordinary wait.
Head Index advances only after the Controller completes the current QCTL operation.
Each Queue Controller interprets its regional Store Head Record, stops its Scheduler Counter on the exact control-cycle boundary and holds the current wait until matching completion.

sourceEvidence.basis: The Controller declares five semantic states.

nodes.description: Advances the local Scheduler Cycle Counter until the regional Store Head reaches its programmed cycle, then dispatches the semantic operation.
Holds arrival asserted until the current barrier round releases this participant.
Blocks on a matching 32-bit Event TAG; mismatched tags do not retire the record.
Holds NOTIFY until all configured participants have arrived and the barrier accepts the notifier.
Holds the 32-bit packet ordinal stable until the external packet-retired indication.
Controller scheduler_counter_ce outputs directly gate 208 MEM and 20 MXM stream-local 32-bit counters. These counters live inside the FU subsystems, not inside QCTL System.

sourceEvidence.basis: Each MEM bank-local issue path owns a 32-bit QCTL Scheduler Cycle Counter.
Each MXM stream owns a 32-bit QCTL Scheduler Cycle Counter.

nodes.description: Two MEM hemispheres × 104 bank-local frontend/queue paths.
Four MXM subsystems × Load, Compute, Dequant, Param Load and Backend stream paths.

The independent Runtime Fabric keeps Event, SYNC, NOTIFY and MEM_PACKET traffic outside the load-time Relay path. Arrivals are accumulated per round; an early NOTIFY waits for every participant, then one Release pulse clears the round.

sourceEvidence.basis: The runtime Fabric owns SYNC/NOTIFY routing independently from Record loading.

nodes.description: Defines exactly which Queue endpoints belong to the current barrier round.
Repeated arrival assertions set the same bit and do not create historical tokens.
NOTIFY remains blocked until all configured participants have arrived.
A one-cycle Release is broadcast to all participants, then the round is cleared without leakage.
Retains early events in eight TAG slots. A matching TAG is broadcast and releases every Controller currently waiting for that same TAG.

sourceEvidence.basis: The same matching TAG broadcast releases every waiter for that TAG.
Unmatched early events are retained in the Event Buffer.

nodes.description: An event may arrive before its waiter and remains buffered until consumed.
One matching TAG simultaneously releases all Controllers waiting for that TAG.
The Controller holds a non-zero 32-bit packet ordinal stable until mem_packet_retired_i. This is packet/data-movement completion and must not be presented as an SRAM Commit.

sourceEvidence.basis: MEM_PACKET validates a non-zero operand and exposes it as the packet ordinal.
MEMPACKET_WAIT holds the ordinal until mem_packet_retired_i.

nodes.description: The ordinal is latched when the Controller enters MEMPACKET_WAIT and remains unchanged while blocked.
External DMA/data movement owns retirement generation. QCTL consumes the final completion indication.

nodes.displayName: Formal Endpoint Map · MEM + MXM Only
nodes.description: The 228 formal QCTL endpoints are exactly 208 MEM bank-local paths and 20 MXM stream-local paths. VXM and SXM are intentionally outside the current formal Queue numbering and direct counter-control chain.
Two hemispheres × 104 bank-local MEM frontend/queue/counter paths.
One Load path per MXM.
One Dequant path per MXM.
One Compute path per MXM.
One Param Load path per MXM.
One Backend path per MXM.
No formal VXM QCTL endpoint or direct QCTL scheduler-counter CE mapping exists in the current cluster integration.
The SXM native Program/ROW path is integrated, but no formal SXM QCTL endpoint or direct QCTL scheduler-counter CE mapping exists in the current cluster integration.

interfaces.name: iMEM Request / Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: Ready/valid request and response path between local instruction memory and fetch.

sourceEvidence.basis: Explicit request/response port bindings.

interfaces.name: Macro Word FIFO → Macro Decoder
interfaces.semanticDescription: 97-bit FIFO entry supplies 96-bit word plus last marker to lpu_mem_macro_decoder.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro decoder consumes word FIFO output.

interfaces.name: Macro Decoder → Context FIFO
interfaces.semanticDescription: Decoded instruction, cycle/count/interval/stride/target/address fields are packed into a 271-bit context.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context concatenation is explicit RTL.

interfaces.name: Context FIFO → Macro Scheduler
interfaces.semanticDescription: Context FIFO output fields feed scheduler context ports.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context FIFO output is unpacked into scheduler fields.

interfaces.name: iMEM Fetch → Macro Pipeline
interfaces.semanticDescription: 96-bit word plus valid/ready/last enters the macro Word FIFO and decoder.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fetch word ports bind directly into u_macro_frontend.

interfaces.name: Validated Context Admission
interfaces.semanticDescription: context_admit_fire writes the first free Active Context slot.

interfaces.name: Next Issue Cycle Match
interfaces.semanticDescription: All Active Context next-cycle fields are compared with schedule_cycle_i.

interfaces.name: Direct MEM64 Issue
interfaces.semanticDescription: The selected Context drives mem_issue_valid/instruction/cycle directly; no independent Instruction Queue exists.

sourceEvidence.basis: Direct mem_issue_* assignments.

interfaces.name: Macro Scheduler → MEM64 / Native32 Adapter
interfaces.semanticDescription: 104 Bank-local Scheduler outputs form the local_issue_* vector; lpu_mem_subsystem selects it and feeds one adapter per lane without an intervening Instruction Queue.

sourceEvidence.basis: local_issue_* directly selects execution_issue_* when the local frontend is enabled.

interfaces.name: Decode / Control → MEM Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only legal and implemented MEM64 operations are adapted into private Native32 commands for the default Native execution array.

sourceEvidence.basis: Adapter emits Native32 only when legal && implemented.

interfaces.name: Implemented Native32 Command
interfaces.semanticDescription: READ and WRITE pass legality/implementation checks and emit one private command.

interfaces.name: Unsupported / Illegal Status
interfaces.semanticDescription: GATHER/SCATTER and opcode2 do not enter Native execution; fault status preserves the distinction between legal-unsupported and illegal.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fault and unsupported outputs are explicit.

interfaces.name: SRF Columns 0..13 ↔ MEM Boundaries 0..13
interfaces.semanticDescription: The integration adapter statically converts ordering between SRF cells and MEM boundary cells without adding state, queueing or arbitration.

interfaces.name: East Direction Mapping
interfaces.semanticDescription: East Write uses the left boundary; East Read produces to the right boundary.

interfaces.name: West Direction Mapping
interfaces.semanticDescription: West Write uses the right boundary; West Read produces to the left boundary.

interfaces.name: SRF Boundary → MEM Write Data
interfaces.semanticDescription: East/West Write selects the direction-correct SRF boundary segment; normal Write consumes it only when valid, while Preserve/WriteTap does not consume.

sourceEvidence.basis: East Write observes left; West Write observes right.

interfaces.name: MEM Registered Read → SRF Injection
interfaces.semanticDescription: One-cycle registered 64-bit leaf reads route to the right boundary for East and the left boundary for West, then enter one of two SRF local producer slots.

sourceEvidence.basis: East Read produces right; West Read produces left.
MEM owns two local SRF injection candidates.

interfaces.name: Target 5 → CTRL Calendar
interfaces.semanticDescription: Program WRITE/PRIME for target 5 and local index 0.

interfaces.name: Target 6 → EXEC Calendar
interfaces.semanticDescription: Program WRITE/PRIME for target 6 and local index 0.

interfaces.name: Absolute-cycle CTRL issue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Configured cycle match issues CTRL on the native ROW path.

interfaces.name: CAP / P / RUN issue
interfaces.semanticDescription: One event may request CAP, P and RUN; core legality and one-stage P timing apply.

interfaces.name: ROW read / write stream
interfaces.semanticDescription: Selectors read the current stream register fabric and write native ROW output through the stream boundary.

interfaces.name: Five stream Schedulers → QCTL gates → Native command ports
interfaces.semanticDescription: The five subsystem-owned Schedulers directly drive Load, Compute, Dequant, Param Load and Backend native ready/valid ports. There is no post-Scheduler Instruction Queue or Local Coordinator.

interfaces.name: Top Column FP32 Results → Static Result Return
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four top-column vectors, each eight FP32 lanes, enter the diagonal return fabric.

interfaces.name: Returned Superlane Vectors → Backend Columns
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four equal-latency returned vectors drive the four independently scheduled backend columns.

interfaces.name: Bottom-Up Row Instruction Wave → Supercell Array
interfaces.semanticDescription: The first launch enters physical bottom Row0 at stage 0, then reaches Row1/2/3 at stage 3/6/9 while moving upward through the 4×4 Supercell array.

interfaces.name: Activation + BF16 Weight → Supercell Array
interfaces.semanticDescription: Activation and weight-forward links are independent horizontal registered paths.

interfaces.name: D3 BF16 Destination Write → Weight Shift Chain
interfaces.semanticDescription: D3 directly writes the selected Supercell weight buffer; no extra output register is inserted.

interfaces.name: Selected 4×4 Cell → Supercell Detail
interfaces.semanticDescription: The visualization reuses the same RTL template for any selected row/column coordinate.

interfaces.name: Double Buffer Weight Groups → 8 Parallel Compute Groups
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each compute group selects one of two eight-weight BF16 group registers; the UI expands all eight parallel groups.

interfaces.name: iMEM Request / Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: Ready/valid request and response path between local instruction memory and fetch.

sourceEvidence.basis: Explicit request/response port bindings.

interfaces.name: Macro Word FIFO → Macro Decoder
interfaces.semanticDescription: 97-bit FIFO entry supplies 96-bit word plus last marker to lpu_mem_macro_decoder.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro decoder consumes word FIFO output.

interfaces.name: Macro Decoder → Context FIFO
interfaces.semanticDescription: Decoded instruction, cycle/count/interval/stride/target/address fields are packed into a 271-bit context.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context concatenation is explicit RTL.

interfaces.name: Context FIFO → Macro Scheduler
interfaces.semanticDescription: Context FIFO output fields feed scheduler context ports.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context FIFO output is unpacked into scheduler fields.

interfaces.name: iMEM Fetch → Macro Pipeline
interfaces.semanticDescription: 96-bit word plus valid/ready/last enters the macro Word FIFO and decoder.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fetch word ports bind directly into u_macro_frontend.

interfaces.name: Validated Context Admission
interfaces.semanticDescription: context_admit_fire writes the first free Active Context slot.

interfaces.name: Next Issue Cycle Match
interfaces.semanticDescription: All Active Context next-cycle fields are compared with schedule_cycle_i.

interfaces.name: Direct MEM64 Issue
interfaces.semanticDescription: The selected Context drives mem_issue_valid/instruction/cycle directly; no independent Instruction Queue exists.

sourceEvidence.basis: Direct mem_issue_* assignments.

interfaces.name: Macro Scheduler → MEM64 / Native32 Adapter
interfaces.semanticDescription: 104 Bank-local Scheduler outputs form the local_issue_* vector; lpu_mem_subsystem selects it and feeds one adapter per lane without an intervening Instruction Queue.

sourceEvidence.basis: local_issue_* directly selects execution_issue_* when the local frontend is enabled.

interfaces.name: Decode / Control → MEM Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only legal and implemented MEM64 operations are adapted into private Native32 commands for the default Native execution array.

sourceEvidence.basis: Adapter emits Native32 only when legal && implemented.

interfaces.name: Implemented Native32 Command
interfaces.semanticDescription: READ and WRITE pass legality/implementation checks and emit one private command.

interfaces.name: Unsupported / Illegal Status
interfaces.semanticDescription: GATHER/SCATTER and opcode2 do not enter Native execution; fault status preserves the distinction between legal-unsupported and illegal.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fault and unsupported outputs are explicit.

interfaces.name: SRF Columns 0..13 ↔ MEM Boundaries 0..13
interfaces.semanticDescription: The integration adapter statically converts ordering between SRF cells and MEM boundary cells without adding state, queueing or arbitration.

interfaces.name: East Direction Mapping
interfaces.semanticDescription: East Write uses the left boundary; East Read produces to the right boundary.

interfaces.name: West Direction Mapping
interfaces.semanticDescription: West Write uses the right boundary; West Read produces to the left boundary.

interfaces.name: SRF Boundary → MEM Write Data
interfaces.semanticDescription: East/West Write selects the direction-correct SRF boundary segment; normal Write consumes it only when valid, while Preserve/WriteTap does not consume.

sourceEvidence.basis: East Write observes left; West Write observes right.

interfaces.name: MEM Registered Read → SRF Injection
interfaces.semanticDescription: One-cycle registered 64-bit leaf reads route to the right boundary for East and the left boundary for West, then enter one of two SRF local producer slots.

sourceEvidence.basis: East Read produces right; West Read produces left.
MEM owns two local SRF injection candidates.

interfaces.name: Five stream Schedulers → QCTL gates → Native command ports
interfaces.semanticDescription: The five subsystem-owned Schedulers directly drive Load, Compute, Dequant, Param Load and Backend native ready/valid ports. There is no post-Scheduler Instruction Queue or Local Coordinator.

interfaces.name: Top Column FP32 Results → Static Result Return
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four top-column vectors, each eight FP32 lanes, enter the diagonal return fabric.

interfaces.name: Returned Superlane Vectors → Backend Columns
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four equal-latency returned vectors drive the four independently scheduled backend columns.

interfaces.name: Bottom-Up Row Instruction Wave → Supercell Array
interfaces.semanticDescription: The first launch enters physical bottom Row0 at stage 0, then reaches Row1/2/3 at stage 3/6/9 while moving upward through the 4×4 Supercell array.

interfaces.name: Activation + BF16 Weight → Supercell Array
interfaces.semanticDescription: Activation and weight-forward links are independent horizontal registered paths.

interfaces.name: D3 BF16 Destination Write → Weight Shift Chain
interfaces.semanticDescription: D3 directly writes the selected Supercell weight buffer; no extra output register is inserted.

interfaces.name: Selected 4×4 Cell → Supercell Detail
interfaces.semanticDescription: The visualization reuses the same RTL template for any selected row/column coordinate.

interfaces.name: Double Buffer Weight Groups → 8 Parallel Compute Groups
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each compute group selects one of two eight-weight BF16 group registers; the UI expands all eight parallel groups.

interfaces.name: Frontend / local entry → 指令译码
interfaces.semanticDescription: Architectural handoff only: the direct boundary is real, while the local load adapter remains unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Resident Local / Global Issue → VXM Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: Eight local issue vectors and one global configuration vector feed the explicit VXM control instance.

interfaces.name: VXM Control → Vector Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Registered configuration waves and execute pulses drive the vector tiles and stream data path.

interfaces.name: Resident Issue → VXM Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: Eight local issue vectors and one global config vector enter the explicit control instance.

interfaces.name: Configure Wave → Fixed Execute Pulse
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four-row registered configuration is followed by a one-cycle, non-retriable execute pulse when the destination Tile is ready.

interfaces.name: Hemisphere Stream Ingress
interfaces.semanticDescription: Both hemisphere boundaries enter the direction-aware bridge.

interfaces.name: Direction-selected Tile Inputs
interfaces.semanticDescription: The global flow-direction bit selects which hemisphere side supplies each Tile while stream numbers remain fixed.

interfaces.name: Private LUT Responses
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each Tile issues 4 Function × 8 Lane requests to its own private 32-SRAM LUT array.

interfaces.name: Tile Results → Opposite Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: Produced vectors are placed on the opposite hemisphere side according to the registered direction.

interfaces.name: Vector Results → MEM
interfaces.semanticDescription: east_to_mem valid/data vectors leave the central bridge.

interfaces.name: Central Direct → VXM Program Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: The real Program Boundary is connected through the Relay-bypass route, but Ready remains zero and the missing adapter prevents endpoint integration.
notes: Boundary Connected / Endpoint Not Integrated · Ready=0 · No Commit.

interfaces.name: Missing Adapter → Standalone Macro Frontend
interfaces.semanticDescription: Intentional gap: the standalone frontend unit test does not establish a Program Load connection.

interfaces.name: Simulation-only Program Bytes
interfaces.semanticDescription: Conceptual association only: the testbench supplies bytes that stand in for an external program image.
notes: No memory-array or DDR timing behavior is modeled.

interfaces.name: Request Contract → Future Adapter
interfaces.semanticDescription: An external integration layer must translate the generic request contract into the selected memory-fabric protocol.

interfaces.name: Future Adapter → Response Contract
interfaces.semanticDescription: An external integration layer must return generic response beats to the Instruction DMA.

interfaces.name: Reserve Request ID
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each accepted request enqueues its ID before the external request is considered accepted.

interfaces.name: Program Read Request
interfaces.semanticDescription: After an outstanding ID slot is reserved, the accepted loader command is presented on the generic external Program DMA request contract.

interfaces.name: Response Beat Enqueue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each accepted response beat enters the 16-entry, 298-bit response FIFO.

interfaces.name: Response ID / Error Check
interfaces.semanticDescription: The accepted response ID is checked against the oldest outstanding ID; error is checked in parallel.

interfaces.name: Buffered Program Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: The response FIFO head is exposed to Program Load reassembly.

interfaces.name: DMA Fault Status
interfaces.semanticDescription: ID mismatch or external response error becomes a terminal fault until reset.

interfaces.name: DMA → 响应缓冲
interfaces.semanticDescription: Instruction DMA accepts and buffers the external response record before reassembly.

interfaces.name: 缓冲 → Assembler
interfaces.semanticDescription: Buffered response bytes and valid-byte keep information enter lpu_program_load_reassembler.

interfaces.name: Assembler → Word FIFO
interfaces.semanticDescription: The Reassembler emits one Program Word record into the explicit eight-entry FIFO.

interfaces.name: Word FIFO → Elastic Stage
interfaces.semanticDescription: WRITE/PRIME handoff details are contained inside this boundary; the architectural main chain crosses from the load-system Word FIFO into the Distributor Elastic Stage.

interfaces.name: Elastic Stage → Relay Chain
interfaces.semanticDescription: Scope/Destination routing feeds the West and East seven-stage Relay chains.

interfaces.name: Relay Chain → FU Frontends / local iMEM
interfaces.semanticDescription: Relay-local records terminate at MEM/MXM frontends and reach the SXM boundary; integration status remains endpoint-specific.

interfaces.name: VXM Direct · Elastic / Distributor → Frontend Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: The VXM route is selected from the Distributor elastic head and bypasses both Relay chains. The VXM subsystem boundary is real, but the local load adapter remains unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Command Descriptor Write
interfaces.semanticDescription: Host fields write one complete Program command descriptor.

interfaces.name: Descriptor Fetch / Command PC
interfaces.semanticDescription: The command PC selects and captures one descriptor before any external valid asserts.

interfaces.name: DMA Command · Address / Length / ID
interfaces.semanticDescription: A load descriptor launches source address, byte count and DMA ID into the Instruction DMA.

interfaces.name: Image Context Enqueue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Scope, Destination and image context pair with the matching response stream.

interfaces.name: DMA Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: Buffered response data, byte keep, last, response ID and error leave the DMA stage.

interfaces.name: Program Response Bytes + Valid-byte Mask
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only response bytes selected by response_keep enter the 64-byte reservoir.

interfaces.name: Image Context + Route Metadata
interfaces.semanticDescription: The dequeued context establishes format, image boundaries and route metadata.

interfaces.name: Compacted Bytes → Program Word
interfaces.semanticDescription: The builder consumes 12 or 16 compacted bytes for the next logical instruction word.

interfaces.name: Program Word
interfaces.semanticDescription: The complete Program Word record enters the explicit eight-entry FIFO.

interfaces.name: Word FIFO Dequeue + Route Metadata
interfaces.semanticDescription: load_word_* supplies WRITE data and route metadata to the handoff mux.

interfaces.name: Deferred PRIME Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: After loading completes, the deferred target selects a PRIME record.

interfaces.name: Distributor Input Handshake
interfaces.semanticDescription: The selected record enters the two-entry elastic stage.

interfaces.name: Buffered Program Load Record
interfaces.semanticDescription: The elastic head exposes Control, payload, Scope and Destination to route predicates.

interfaces.name: West Record
interfaces.semanticDescription: West transmits one concrete Program Record.

interfaces.name: East Record
interfaces.semanticDescription: East transmits one concrete Program Record.

interfaces.name: West R0–R6
interfaces.semanticDescription: West enters W0 and traverses seven registered stages.

interfaces.name: East R0–R6
interfaces.semanticDescription: East enters E0 and traverses seven registered stages.

interfaces.name: Integrated MEM / MXM Frontends
interfaces.semanticDescription: Relay-local records terminate in integrated MEM/MXM local iMEM/frontend paths.

interfaces.name: SXM / VXM Program Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: Real subsystem boundaries are connected; local load adapters remain unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Commit
interfaces.semanticDescription: Accepted integrated writes return ordered status.

interfaces.name: START
interfaces.semanticDescription: Controller lifecycle starts integrated FU-local frontends.

interfaces.name: Fault
interfaces.semanticDescription: Endpoint and frontend faults return to lifecycle control.

interfaces.name: Program Reset / Transport Flush
interfaces.semanticDescription: Program Reset clears transport and frontend state.

interfaces.name: Load Manager → East / West Relay Chains
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only load-time Partition and Record packets traverse the Relay chains; Queue ID selects Hemisphere, Relay and local Queue slot.

interfaces.name: Regional Store Head → FU-local Endpoint
interfaces.semanticDescription: Endpoint Head Index/Generation selects the owning Store entry; the Store returns Loaded/Valid/Record/Error in parallel for all formal Queues.

interfaces.name: Endpoint Head → Five-State Controller
interfaces.semanticDescription: The Endpoint exposes the current valid regional Head Record and advances only after semantic retirement.

interfaces.name: Controller CE → FU-local Scheduler Counter
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each Controller independently advances or freezes its mapped MEM/MXM Scheduler Cycle Counter.

interfaces.name: Runtime Barrier Arrival / Release
interfaces.semanticDescription: Controllers publish arrivals and receive one-cycle release through the independent Runtime Fabric.

interfaces.name: Event TAG Broadcast
interfaces.semanticDescription: The Event Buffer broadcasts a matching TAG to every Controller waiting for that TAG.

interfaces.name: MEM_PACKET Ordinal / Retire
interfaces.semanticDescription: QCTL presents a stable ordinal and waits for external packet retirement; this is not an SRAM Commit signal.

evidence.expression: one native Program/ROW subsystem per Hemisphere
MEM, MXM and SXM are organized per hemisphere; VXM is a single central subsystem
Macro Scheduler drives the native command ready/valid boundary directly; no post-Scheduler Instruction Queue
104 bank-local Frontends per hemisphere; Scheduler outputs feed the lane adapter directly
Distribution System instantiates East + West chains and each chain generates seven Relay stages
14 Distribution handshakes and one-Hemisphere seven-way iMEM writes verified
distributed QCTL store plus 228 FU-local endpoints
two chains, seven regional stores per hemisphere

controlDomain.relationship: Separate encoding domain from FU instruction opcodes

evidence.expression: 2-bit Scope + 13-bit Destination travel with every Program Word; no Sequence ID field

values.name: EAST
values.meaning: Send to the concrete East endpoint.

values.name: WEST
values.meaning: Send to the concrete West endpoint.

values.name: BOTH
values.meaning: Distributor expands one record into independent East and West handshakes.

scope.relationship: Scope controls fanout. It is not part of the 13-bit Destination and is not an FU instruction field.

fields.name: Target Kind
fields.meaning: MEM, five MXM stream classes, VXM or legacy-reserved SXM kinds.

states.name: IDLE
states.statement: Reads the current Head Record and keeps CE high only for nonblocking or already-completed work.

states.name: SYNC_WAIT
states.statement: Holds the Queue until the Participant-Mask Barrier broadcasts Release.

states.name: EVENT_WAIT
states.statement: Holds the Queue until the 32-bit TAG Event broadcast matches the saved operand.

states.name: NOTIFY_WAIT
states.statement: Keeps an early NOTIFY request asserted; retirement waits for the current round to release.

states.name: MEMPACKET_WAIT
states.statement: Keeps the packet ordinal stable until external mem_packet_retired_i.

barrier.participantMask: Only Queue IDs selected by participant_mask_i participate in the current barrier round.
barrier.arrival: Arrival is an idempotent per-round bit mask, not a token counter.
barrier.notify: An early NOTIFY remains pending and cannot retire before every configured participant arrives.
barrier.release: A successful NOTIFY emits one-cycle Release directly to all participants.
barrier.roundIsolation: Arrival state is cleared on Release and held clear across the Release edge, so consecutive rounds do not leak history.

eventBuffer.statement: The independent Event Buffer retains early DMA completion TAGs outside every Controller; one matching TAG broadcast may release every waiting Controller with that TAG.

memPacket.retirement: MEM_PACKET ordinal remains stable while waiting and retires only through external mem_packet_retired_i.
memPacket.sramCommitRelationship: Packet retirement is not SRAM Commit. QCTL consumes only the final data-completion event; generation of the final SRAM Commit event remains in DMA / data movement.

pipeline.title: MEM Macro Scheduler · Context Expansion Pipeline
pipeline.summary: The MEM Scheduler validates and converts the Context FIFO head, admits it directly into an originally free Active Context slot, then selects work ahead of the absolute issue cycle and directly emits one MEM64 instruction plus issue cycle. outer_cycle_transition advances from the previous row final issue to the next row first issue; outer_spatial_transition applies the matching address or operand transition.
pipeline.inputLabel: 271 bit Context · ready/valid from Context FIFO
pipeline.outputLabel: 64 bit instruction + 32-bit issue cycle → MEM64 / Native32 adapter
pipeline.timingNote: Registered ownership boundaries are the upstream Context FIFO and Active Context state. The MEM Scheduler has no second ingress register and no independent post-Scheduler output queue: context_admit_fire is the direct Context FIFO handshake into an originally free Active Context slot. Active Context advances only on schedule_select_fire, when the downstream adapter accepts the issue handshake. outer_cycle_transition advances from the previous row final issue to the next row first issue; outer_spatial_transition applies the matching address or operand transition.
